source: All-In Podcast — GPT-5 underwhelms, AI TAM/ROIC/energy, China's advantage, tariffs, Nvidia chip smuggling, Apple buybacks and AI strategy
summary: Resuming sales of downgraded Nvidia chips (H20/B50-equivalent) to China was the right policy move — legalizing a lower-potency product reduces black market demand for the high-end chips.
summary_extended: Baker argues that the Trump administration's decision to resume sales of downgraded Nvidia chips (H20 and a de-specced Blackwell equivalent) to China was a strategically sound policy move. His reasoning draws on a drug legalization analogy: by making a legal, lower-potency product available, you reduce the black market incentive to smuggle the higher-end, more restricted chips (like the full H100/H200 or top-tier Blackwell). Baker had previously called this 'very smart' and reaffirms that view here, framing it as both geopolitically sensible and commercially rational. The direct investment implication is positive for Nvidia, which stands to recover meaningful China revenue from H20 and downgraded Blackwell sales that had been cut off by prior export restrictions. No specific revenue figures or timelines are cited, but the near-term benefit to Nvidia's data center segment from reopened China demand is the clear takeaway.
